data.title: Have Assurant Insiders Been Selling Stock?
data.description:
We wouldn't blame Assurant, Inc. (NYSE:AIZ) shareholders if they were a little worried about the fact that Ryan Lumsden, a company insider, recently netted about US$1.2m selling shares at an average price of US$319. That's a big disposal, and it decreased their holding size by 23%, which is notable but not too bad.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Assurant Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

In fact, the recent sale by Ryan Lumsden was the biggest sale of Assurant shares made by an insider individual in the last twelve months, according to our records. That means that an insider was selling shares at below the current price (US$322). As a general rule we consider it to be discouraging when insiders are selling below the current price, because it suggests they were happy with a lower valuation. While insider selling is not a positive sign, we can't be sure if it does mean insiders think the shares are fully valued, so it's only a weak sign. It is worth noting that this sale was only 23% of Ryan Lumsden's holding.

In the last year Assurant insiders didn't buy any company stock. You can see the insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year depicted in the chart below. If you click on the chart, you can see all the individual transactions, including the share price, individual, and the date!

View our latest analysis for Assurant

I will like Assurant better if I see some big insider buys. While we wait, check out this free list of undervalued and small cap stocks with considerable, recent, insider buying.

Insider Ownership

Looking at the total insider shareholdings in a company can help to inform your view of whether they are well aligned with common shareholders. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. It appears that Assurant insiders own 0.6% of the company, worth about US$100m. While this is a strong but not outstanding level of insider ownership, it's enough to indicate some alignment between management and smaller shareholders.

So What Do The Assurant Insider Transactions Indicate?

An insider sold Assurant shares recently, but they didn't buy any. Looking to the last twelve months, our data doesn't show any insider buying. But since Assurant is profitable and growing, we're not too worried by this. Insider ownership isn't particularly high, so this analysis makes us cautious about the company. So we'd only buy after careful consideration. In addition to knowing about insider transactions going on, it's beneficial to identify the risks facing Assurant. data.title: We're Hopeful That IZEA Worldwide (NASDAQ:IZEA) Will Use Its Cash Wisely
data.description:
There's no doubt that money can be made by owning shares of unprofitable businesses. For example, biotech and mining exploration companies often lose money for years before finding success with a new treatment or mineral discovery. But while the successes are well known, investors should not ignore the very many unprofitable companies that simply burn through all their cash and collapse.

So should IZEA Worldwide (NASDAQ:IZEA) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purposes of this article, cash burn is the annual rate at which an unprofitable company spends cash to fund its growth; its negative free cash flow. First, we'll determine its cash runway by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

When Might IZEA Worldwide Run Out Of Money?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. As at June 2026, IZEA Worldwide had cash of US$47m and no debt. In the last year, its cash burn was US$2.6m. That means it had a cash runway of very many years as of June 2026. Even though this is but one measure of the company's cash burn, the thought of such a long cash runway warms our bellies in a comforting way. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

See our latest analysis for IZEA Worldwide

How Well Is IZEA Worldwide Growing?

Notably, IZEA Worldwide actually ramped up its cash burn very hard and fast in the last year, by 127%, signifying heavy investment in the business. While that's concerning on it's own, the fact that operating revenue was actually down 27% over the same period makes us positively tremulous. In light of the above-mentioned, we're pretty wary of the trajectory the company seems to be on. In reality, this article only makes a short study of the company's growth data. You can take a look at how IZEA Worldwide has developed its business over time by checking this visualization of its revenue and earnings history.

How Hard Would It Be For IZEA Worldwide To Raise More Cash For Growth?

While IZEA Worldwide seems to be in a fairly good position, it's still worth considering how easily it could raise more cash, even just to fuel faster growth. Companies can raise capital through either debt or equity. Commonly, a business will sell new shares in itself to raise cash and drive growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

IZEA Worldwide's cash burn of US$2.6m is about 6.8% of its US$38m market capitalisation. That's a low proportion, so we figure the company would be able to raise more cash to fund growth, with a little dilution, or even to simply borrow some money.

So, Should We Worry About IZEA Worldwide's Cash Burn?

On this analysis of IZEA Worldwide's cash burn, we think its cash runway was reassuring, while its increasing cash burn has us a bit worried. While we're the kind of investors who are always a bit concerned about the risks involved with cash burning companies, the metrics we have discussed in this article leave us relatively comfortable about IZEA Worldwide's situation. On another note, IZEA Worldwide has 2 warning signs (and 1 which is concerning) we think you should know about.

data.title: Procter & Gamble (PG) Debuts Crest Toothpaste For Gum Bleeding
data.description:
• Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) has launched a new Crest toothpaste that uses hops β-acids to address gum bleeding.
  • The formulation combines hops β-acids with an updated thickener technology that Procter & Gamble describes as a major oral care advance.
  • P&G cites strong clinical results for the Crest hops β-acids toothpaste, positioning it alongside earlier step-change developments in gum health products.
  • This new Crest hops β-acids toothpaste is only part of the story for Procter & Gamble's oral care strategy. We have also spotted 2 warning signs worth knowing about at Procter & Gamble.

Procter & Gamble, a US based supplier of branded consumer packaged goods, uses its scale in everyday categories like oral care to test new science based formulas that can then be rolled out across its Crest franchise and broader hygiene portfolio.

How could this Crest hops β acids toothpaste matter for Procter & Gamble’s market opportunity?

The new Crest formula targets gum bleeding with an Activ Bio Cleanser system that P&G says cuts bleeding by two thirds or more within two weeks in trials. That pushes the brand deeper into oral health territory rather than just cosmetic whitening. This opens more room in higher value therapeutic style toothpaste segments where shoppers often accept premium pricing.

The launch lines up closely with the existing Narrative that leans on product superiority and AI assisted R&D to support organic sales and brand strength. Any disclosed share gains versus Gum Detoxify or updates on gum health product penetration in 2027 earnings calls will be the clearest markers.
